findings:
🔴 [deny-dir-descendants] MUST-FIX Denial is evaluated only on leaf paths, while directory removal handles only literal patterns ending in `/**`; consequently `logs/x.raw.log/verdict.txt` or `docs/plans/p.review.md/body` survives in both `tree/` and `diff.patch` although its ancestor directory matches a default deny pattern. Derive directory prefixes and treat every descendant of a matched directory as denied for tree, diff, rename, and symlink-target processing.
🟠 [ambient-common-gitdir] MUST-FIX `gitEnv` preserves ambient `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, which can make the supposedly isolated temporary `GIT_DIR` consume another repository's config and `info/attributes`, allowing a smudge/filter command to run before integrity verification. Scrub `GIT_COMMON_DIR` from every Git subprocess environment and add a poisoned-environment sentinel test.
🟠 [attributes-symlink-type] MUST-FIX Every `.gitattributes` blob is restored with `writeFileSync`, so a safe tracked `.gitattributes` symlink becomes a regular file and then fails integrity instead of being retained as required. Restore removed attribute entries according to their Git mode, using a real symlink for mode `120000`, before integrity and hazard pruning.
🟠 [name-status-utf8] MUST-FIX `parseNameStatus` decodes old and new path buffers without UTF-8 validation, so a deleted or renamed invalid-UTF-8 path present only in the base tree is lossily decoded and accepted after checkout. Validate every `--name-status -z` path buffer and fail with `unsupported path encoding: <hex>` before creating or checking out the packet tree.
🟠 [posix-backslash-path] MUST-FIX `packetPathDenied` rewrites backslashes to `/` even though Git paths and the deny grammar are repository-relative POSIX byte strings; on POSIX a valid root file such as `.qc\product.js` is therefore falsely treated as being under `.qc/` and silently omitted from review. Match canonical Git paths without rewriting backslashes.
